Io. 20, 1.''}} {{verse|chapter=16|verse=2}} {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text={{sc|Easter day}}.}}And very early the fir{{ls}}t of the Sabboths, they come to the monument: the {{ls}}unne being novv ri{{ls}}en. {{verse|chapter=16|verse=3}} And they {{ls}}aid one to an other, VVho {{ls}}hal roll vs backe the {{ls}}tone from the doore of the monument? {{verse|chapter=16|verse=4}} And looking, they {{ls}}avv the {{ls}}tone rolled backe. for it vvas very great. {{verse|chapter=16|verse=5}} And entring into the monument, they {{ls}}avv a yong man {{ls}}itting on the right hand, couered vvith a vvhite robe: and they vvere a{{ls}}tonied. {{verse|chapter=16|verse=6}} VVho {{ls}}aith to them, Be not di{{ls}}maied: you {{ls}}eeke {{sc|Iesvs}} of Nazareth, that vvas crucified: he is ri{{ls}}en, he is not here, behold the place vvhere they laid him. {{verse|chapter=16|verse=7}} But goe, tel his Di{{ls}}ciples and {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Peter is named in {{ls}}pecial (as often els where) for prerogatiue.}}∷ Peter that he goeth before you into Galilee: there you {{ls}}hal {{ls}}ee him, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mr. 14, 28.''}}* as he told you.⊣ {{verse|chapter=16|verse=8}} But they going forth, fled from the monument. for trembling and feare had inuaded them: and they {{ls}}aid nothing to any body. for they vvere afraid.

{{verse|chapter=16|verse=9}} And he ri{{ls}}ing early the fir{{ls}}t of the Sabboth, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Io. 20, 16.''}}* appeared fir{{ls}}t to Marie Magdalene, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Luc. 8, 2.''}}* out of vvhom he had ca{{ls}}t {{ls}}euen deuils. {{verse|chapter=16|verse=10}} She vvent and told them that had been vvith him, that vvere mourning and vveeping. {{verse|chapter=16|verse=11}} And they hearing that he vvas aliue and had been {{ls}}een of her, did not beleeue.
